What We Do

Restoration services built around natural stone.

Every surface is different — we assess the stone, the wear, and the finish before recommending a process.

01

Marble Restoration

Full restoration of marble floors, countertops and vanities — removing dullness, etching and years of wear.

02

Granite Restoration

Restoring shine and structural integrity to granite countertops and surfaces without damaging the stone.

03

Travertine Repair

Filling, leveling and refinishing travertine — indoors and out — for a smooth, consistent surface.

04

Honing & Refinishing

Correcting etching, scratches and uneven texture to restore a smooth, even finish.

05

Stone Polishing

Machine polishing that brings back natural shine and reflectivity across marble, granite and travertine.

06

Crack & Chip Repair

Precision repair of cracks, chips and cosmetic damage, blended to match the surrounding stone.

07

Stone Installation

Professional installations of natural stone countertops, vanities, and custom stone surfaces.

08

Stone Fabrication

Custom cutting, shaping, and finishing of stone for a precise fit and clean finish.

FAQ

Common questions.

Straight answers about natural stone care and how we work. Don't see your question? Call or text 201-675-6568.

What types of stone do you work with?

Marble, granite and travertine make up most of our work, along with other natural stone. Not sure what you have? Send a few photos and we'll help identify it.

What's the difference between honing and polishing?

Honing uses fine abrasives to smooth the surface — removing etching and light scratches and leaving a matte or satin finish. Polishing goes a step further, refining the stone until it has a reflective shine. Many restorations involve both.

Can etching and dull spots be removed?

Usually, yes. Etching — the dull marks acidic liquids and cleaners leave on marble and travertine — can typically be removed by honing and re-polishing the affected area. Deeper damage can take more work, which we'll explain once we've seen it.

How often should stone be sealed?

It depends on the stone, its finish and how much use it gets, so there's no single schedule. A simple check: if a few drops of water darken the stone within a few minutes, it's likely time to reseal.

Can cracks and chips be repaired?

Many can. Cracks and chips are often filled, color-blended to match the surrounding stone and refinished. How well a repair blends depends on its size, location and the stone itself, so photos help us give you an honest assessment.

Do you take on residential and commercial work?

Yes — from single countertops and vanities to lobbies, elevators and larger floors.

What areas do you serve?

New Jersey, New York City and the surrounding areas. If you're just outside that range, reach out anyway.

How do I get an estimate?

Call or text 201-675-6568, or use the estimate form below with a few photos of the surface. We'll review the details and follow up.
